title: Browser Wallet Privacy: Can Your Crypto Addresses Leak Without a Transaction?
keyQuestions: Can a website see my crypto wallet address without me sending a transaction?
Can browser wallet extensions create privacy leaks before a transaction?
Can RPC traffic link several addresses to the same wallet environment?
Does disconnecting a dApp remove all wallet-related privacy exposure?
How is wallet-provider fingerprinting different from ordinary browser fingerprinting?
Can a VPN prevent browser wallet tracking?
How can I reduce browser-wallet exposure before a no-KYC crypto swap?
quickSteps: Separate wallet activity from identity-heavy browsing by using a dedicated browser profile or device role.
Divide crypto accounts by purpose so one wallet environment does not automatically connect every financial identity.
Grant account access only when the site genuinely needs it, and expose only the account required for that action.
Review connected sites, wallet permissions, and on-chain token approvals separately instead of assuming Disconnect removed everything.
Prefer a wallet-to-wallet or reduced-browser flow when direct wallet connection adds no practical value to the transaction.

issueRouting.start: What browser-wallet privacy exposure exists before the crypto transaction is sent?

branches.if: A website only needs to show information, a quote, or a deposit address
then: Avoid connecting the browser wallet if account access is not required.
Use the service without exposing an unnecessary wallet provider relationship.
Prefer a wallet-to-wallet or reduced-browser flow when the task supports it.

branches.if: A website genuinely requires wallet connection
then: Expose only the account required for the task when account-level selection is available.
Keep public, experimental, storage, and sensitive wallet roles separate.
Review the wallet permission state after the interaction ends.

branches.if: An old dApp connection or wallet permission may still exist
then: Open the wallet's connected-sites or permissions interface.
Remove relationships that are no longer needed.
Review on-chain token approvals separately because disconnecting a site does not automatically revoke them.

riskNotes: A browser wallet can expose privacy-relevant metadata even when no transaction is sent.
Wallet-provider detection can add a crypto-specific signal to an ordinary browser fingerprint.
RPC or backend queries may reveal relationships between addresses that are not directly linked on-chain.
Old account permissions can create correlation between addresses across later visits if they remain available.
Shared third-party scripts can increase cross-site correlation risk when wallet identifiers become visible.
A VPN or Tor can improve network privacy but cannot automatically hide wallet-provider information or addresses disclosed through wallet permissions.
